items.title: Palantir Q3 2026 earnings (reported Nov 2 after close): $2.313B revenue (+96% YoY), first-ever quarter above $2B, US commercial ($984M, +148% YoY) overtakes US government revenue for the first time
items.summary: Palantir reported Q3 2026 results on November 2, 2026 after market close: total revenue of $2.313B (+96% YoY, +20% QoQ) — the first quarter in company history above $2B — against the $2.160–$2.164B guidance the company set on its Q2 call. GAAP diluted EPS was $0.44 and adjusted EPS was also $0.44, well above the $0.36 analyst consensus Benzinga cited. US commercial revenue reached $984M (+148% YoY) and overtook US government revenue for the first time ever — a long-promised inflection for the AIP (Artificial Intelligence Platform) commercial business. Adjusted operating income was $1.427B against $1.292–$1.296B guidance; cash, equivalents, and Treasuries totaled $10.4B. Secondary coverage reports the Q3 release accompanied two defense-related items — a US Army framework agreement and a UK Ministry of Defence engagement — but the specific contract figures ($10B / £1.5B) that appear in some headlines are summaries of earlier 2025 announcements rebundled with this quarter's print; the SEC 8-K is the authoritative source for new material. On the call, CRO Ryan Taylor framed AIP boot camps as delivering working workflows on customer data in 'five days or less' versus 'one to three months previously,' and management cited a 10x speed gain with 3x fewer resources on reference deployments. The Benzinga transcript carries a specific worked example: two forward-deployed engineers used AIP to migrate a legacy data warehouse in five days versus an estimated two years for a traditional systems-integrator path. Share reaction was mixed in extended trading on valuation concerns — TradingView's GuruFocus relay carries the 'posts record Q3 revenue but shares fall on valuation concerns' framing — and a Q4 2026 revenue guide was raised on the release (specific updated figures should be read off the 8-K Exhibit 99.1 rather than secondary coverage, which conflicts in places).
items.why_it_matters: This is the first quarter in which a pure-play enterprise AI company's commercial revenue has outgrown its government revenue — the inflection the AIP story has been pointed at since Palantir pivoted to generative-AI positioning in 2023. Taken alongside Alphabet's Q3 (Google Cloud +103% YoY to $30.7B, in the Nov 3 am digest) and Apple's Q4 FY2026 (memory-chip-shortage callout, same am), it's a third post-cycle confirmation that AI revenue is no longer early-adopter — it's a material enterprise line. For Gabe's HTML/CSS/Python stack, there are two concrete things worth sitting with. (1) The AIP boot camp pattern is a readable, portable design idea: send forward-deployed engineers directly into a customer's data, deliver a working thin slice in five days, iterate on real workflows rather than architectural diagrams — this is the opposite of the big-bang integration project and maps onto 'ship a working Python prototype against real data in a week' as a personal practice. The 10x-speed / 3x-fewer-resources numbers come from Palantir's own commentary and should be treated as marketing-tinged, but the underlying pattern is sound and widely applicable. (2) AIP's technical core is an ontology layer that abstracts over heterogeneous data sources before any LLM touches them — the same design pattern anyone building a Python-plus-LLM app on messy data ends up reinventing. Palantir's publicly available product documentation on ontology, actions, and functions is the clearest public write-up of this pattern at enterprise scale; the ideas are directly readable and transferable to small Python projects (ontology ≈ Pydantic/typed-domain-model layer, actions ≈ callable tools with permissioned side effects, functions ≈ reusable transforms). The valuation-concerns stock reaction is a separate story — PLTR has been trading at an elevated multiple for most of 2026 — and should not be read as a critique of the underlying business signal. The specific durable number from this print is $984M in US commercial revenue, up 148% YoY: at that growth rate, Palantir's US commercial will annualize past $4B within three quarters, which places AIP as a $4B+ revenue line in a market where Alphabet's $30.7B Cloud and Microsoft's Azure AI are the only comparable scale points for publicly measurable enterprise AI revenue.
items.why_it_matters_brief: Palantir Q3 beats hard with $2.313B — US commercial revenue ($984M, +148% YoY) outruns US government for the first time, the clearest post-cycle sign that enterprise AI is a material revenue line, not a pilot.
